messages.subject: Automatic labeling of max value
parts:
Hi all,

Inspired by this CrossValidated question "How to add a label to the max
value in R's ggplot2?"[1], I was wondering if there is a more
elegant/automatic approach to label the peak of the distribution (than
using annotate()), e.g. via ..count.. . The following example labels all
peaks and I'd like to see only the label "33" (by the way: How can I get
rid of the 0's?).

library(ggplot2)
set.seed(2)
dfr <- data.frame(x=sample(1:8, 200, replace=TRUE))

p <- ggplot(aes(x=x), data=dfr) + geom_freqpoly() +
stat_bin(aes(label=..count..), geom="text", position="identity")
p

Thanks,

Bernd

[1]
http://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/12051/how-to-add-a-label-to-the-max-value-in-rs-ggplot2

I'd do the computation myself:

ggplot(counts, aes(x)) +
geom_freqpoly(aes(weight = freq)) +
geom_text(aes(y = freq, label = freq))

Hadley
